subject: seed-quiz-key.js uses a non-merge .set() and silently wipes explanations/revealToAll/reviewAfterFails
description:
PRE-EXISTING, found 2026-08-07 while wiring poolSize through the write path for #295. functions/seed-quiz-key.js writes with 'await ref.set({...})' and NO {merge:true}, so it REPLACES the whole quiz_keys doc. Its payload carries answers, passingScore, questionCount, note, poolSize and updatedAt -- but NOT explanations, revealToAll or reviewAfterFails, which push-quiz-keys.js does write. So running seed-quiz-key.js on any quiz that already has post-submission review configured silently strips it: students stop seeing correct answers and explanations after submitting, and the reviewAfterFails escape hatch for repeatedly-failing students disappears. Nothing errors and nothing logs it. 122 of 621 registry entries carry revealToAll, so the blast radius is large. NOT fixed as part of #295 because it is a different defect with a different blast radius and deserves its own review: the fix is either merge:true plus explicit deletes (matching push-quiz-keys.js's model, where the registry is authoritative in both directions) or adding the three fields to the payload. Decide which, do not just bolt on merge:true -- the two tools would then disagree about who owns a field.
[2026-08-08 03:40] FIXED in 7f26ce9b5. Blast radius was LARGER than reported: a production field scan found 30+ field names across 621 docs, and the non-merge .set() destroyed all of them (source, createdAt, karlAuditArtifact, fixNote, lastFixedBy, rebalancedAt, shuffled, seedSource, ...), not just the 3 recorded. Resolution: quiz-key-payload.js is now the ONE definition both writers call, and both merge. NOT done, deliberately, and left for the operator: explanations and reviewAfterFails are still non-authoritative (written when present, never deleted) because 4 live openstack quizzes carry them without registry entries, and delete-when-absent would strip post-submission review from quizzes that have it today. push-quiz-keys.js now REPORTS that drift. Proven on the emulator both directions: new code keeps all 8 planted provenance fields, the old non-merge write loses all 8.
